findings.text: Secondary bring-up data pairs a task pointer for the incoming CPU with a long status word observed by the boot coordinator.
MPIDR hashing parameters comprise a 64-bit mask plus four per-affinity shift values and a total bit count governing table sizing.
Hash capacity is a power of two derived from the stored bit count, while logical index resolution scans the architectural identifier map and signals failure when no entry matches.
Logical to physical CPU identifier translation exposes a per-index lookup over the architecture identifier array.

Shared software-generated inter-processor signalling uses one interrupt identity per IPI kind with non-maskable selection decided by a predicate, descriptor publication across the possible-CPU set, and hidden marking.

Locality-based inter-processor signalling uses distinct interrupt identities per CPU and IPI kind with forced per-CPU affinity, non-automatic enabling at request time, hidden plus non-balancing markings, and per-CPU descriptor publication.
Interrupt request and affinity problems during IPI setup surface as warnings with registration continuing, leaving partially configured state observable.
Secondary boot status publication provides ordered visibility to polling observers through a single store plus an inner-shareable barrier.
A parked secondary remains in a low-power event wait, with the panic variant recording a panic boot status as part of entering that wait.
Single-CPU wakeup signalling is intentionally unavailable and fails at build time, while logical CPU teardown is an empty operation without side effects.

Physical memory coverage allows up to fifty-two bits with the active limit linked to the physical mask shift, while sparse section sizing has alternative configurations of twenty-nine and twenty-seven bits.
Hypervisor hardening reserves four exception slots with derived vector area sized from all but one slot times two kilobytes.
Spectre exposure is classified into three mutually exclusive outcomes of unaffected, mitigated, or vulnerable.

Hypervisor exception routing selects among direct entry, direct with hardening bounce, indirect mapping bounce, and indirect with hardening bounce, where direct entry is the zero default used when no mitigation applies.
Per-CPU hardening state pairs the selected hypervisor vector mode with a parameterless callback used for the hardening action.
The post-spinlock barrier is a full memory barrier, and virtual-CPU preemption queries report not preempted.
Early boot guard setup couples randomized per-task guard creation with pointer-authentication enablement, where global guard publication applies only when per-task guards are disabled.
Stack range descriptors carry low and high address bounds used for containment checks.
Unwind cursors hold a frame pointer and program counter plus a current stack range and a reference to a stack-range table with its length.
Frame linkage records hold paired frame pointer and return address values, with an extended form adding a numeric type tag.
Frame metadata tags distinguish untagged, terminal, and register-block carriers with values zero through two respectively.

Firmware, interrupt, overflow, and delegated-exception stack ranges derive from per-CPU bases plus fixed sizes, except the firmware range which extends downward from a global top by thread size, with containment predicates testing a pointer plus length against the derived range and a thread helper testing the current pointer with unit length.
When delegated-exception stacks are unavailable the corresponding range queries degrade to an unknown-stack result.
Frame advancement requires aligned pointers located in known stacks and couples stack-range consumption with single-copy loading of successor frame and return values.
Non-protected hypervisor unwind setup couples common state preparation with caller-provided frame and program seeding.
Second-stage depth has dual derivations from guest size with fixed adjustment and from virtualization control state, with minimum cache sizing one less than depth.

Compatibility file-status layout orders device, mode, link count, ownership, device identifier, size, block sizing and counts, three timestamp pairs, and a 64-bit inode at the end with padding preserving historical placement and a flag noting the broken intermediate inode field.

Static-call trampolines occupy executable trampoline storage branching indirectly through a read-only target cell with branch-target identification, while null and zero-return variants both target the shared zero-return helper.

Architecture string support advertises optimized handling for memory set, copy, move, cache-flushing copy, reverse and forward search, compare, bounded compare, length, bounded length, memory compare, and memory search, with move operations aliased to the internal implementation and fortified variants explicitly disabled.
Suspend context sizing fixes fourteen general context slots and twelve callee-saved slots.
Suspend state combines a sixteen-byte aligned array of context words plus stack pointer with a sleep wrapper adding callee-saved storage, required to match low-level save and restore ordering.
Synchronized bit operations are direct aliases of the standard atomic bit primitives and word compare-exchange.

Call identity is carried in a dedicated number field, with rollback restoring the first result register from the saved original argument, result extraction sign-extending for compatibility threads, error extraction yielding zero for non-error values, and result installation truncating to thirty-two bits for compatibility threads.
A negative-one call number denotes suppressed dispatch with a forced not-implemented error result.
First-argument authority rests in the saved original on read, while writes keep live registers and saved original coherent so later reads observe the new first parameter.
Call-type callbacks receive read-only trap registers and produce a long result, while audit architecture reporting distinguishes compatibility threads from native 64-bit threads.

Native call wrappers combine saved-original first-parameter sourcing with length handling, type conversion, validation, and result protection plus error-injection support, while zero-argument and conditional forms cover metadata and weakly defaulted unimplemented handling.

Compatibility call wrappers combine six live-register sourcing with delousing plus error-injection support, while zero-argument and conditional forms mirror native behavior for the compatibility namespace.
System instruction encoding fixes CRm shift 8 mask 15, Op2 shift 5 mask 7, Op0 shift 19 mask 3, CRn shift 12 mask 15, and Op1 shift 16 mask 7.
System instruction encoding aliases instruction and register forms with a helper extracting the Op2 subfield.

Processor-state field construction combines operation subfields with immediate position tied to the CRm shift, covering tag checking, user access, access control, data-independent timing, and speculation barriers, each with emission and inline setter support.

Instruction emission adapts to assembler capabilities with direct and stringified forms for both native and byte-swapped 32-bit encodings, where the swapped form reverses byte order and the native form is identity.
